articles.title: Game, set and tache: Carlos Alcaraz joins growing trend for a stylish top lip
articles.summary: Tennis superstar is latest celebrity to sport a ‘refined’ moustache which owes little to bushy Tom Selleck look. The tennis superstar Carlos Alcaraz might have been knocked out of the Shanghai Masters in straight sets earlier this week, but he did so sporting a moustache that became almost as…
body: “I always wanted to step on the court at least once with the moustache,” Alcaraz said. The Spaniard and his team had all agreed to take the facial-hair plunge if he won the Japan Open, which he did for a second straight year. “¡Bigotes para todos!” or “moustaches for everyone”, they apparently cheered at the end of the match.
At Milan fashion week last month, the Wuthering Heights star Jacob Elordi sported a thin strip of hair on his top lip as he watched his girlfriend, Kendall Jenner, model for the Bottega Veneta show.

A moustachioed Harry Styles is roughly halfway through his record-breaking 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York. The actor Timothée Chalamet, who kept his Marty Supreme ’tache on throughout awards season, has been playing around with his facial hair again, adding a goatee.
On TikTok, gen Z men with moustaches are plentiful, as are tutorials for how to grow and style them – alongside almost as many videos from older generations questioning them.

articles.title: British Cycling under scrutiny over allegations of ‘toxic culture’ in leadership team
articles.summary: Former employee alleges bullying swept under carpet. British Cycling defends handling of complaints. British Cycling is facing further questions after a former employee accused it of having a “toxic culture” days after Matt Richardson was sent home from the World Track Championships in Shanghai.
body: Jack Lindsay, who worked as a commercial manager at British Cycling from 2024 to 2025, criticised the way he claimed it responded to his formal workplace bullying complaint spanning dozens of incidents. And he also questioned what he branded a lack of oversight from UK Sport, which has given the organisation £30m to prepare for the LA Olympics.

“The complaint covered dozens of incidents over six months, spanning multiple categories of alleged bullying,” Lindsay wrote in a post on LinkedIn. “Most were partially substantiated. There would be no apology, and I was told of no action against the individual I had sought to hold responsible.”

Lindsay also claimed that he had “repeatedly raised incidents of bullying by a member of the executive with members of the senior leadership team, and that management had chosen to address them informally”.
“It is not acceptable to continue subjecting staff to a leadership team that have perpetuated this toxic culture,” he said.

articles.title: Do Manchester City have any grounds to win their appeal?
articles.summary: Manchester City face "substantial hurdles" to overcome if they are to have any chance of winning their appeal after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, a leading lawyer has told BBC Sport.
body: City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, and creating "sham contracts" to inflate sponsorship deals by £830m.

The club have said they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and they have "irrefutable evidence" the ruling "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".
In their appeal, City will argue the payments were made by the United Arab Emirates government as a shareholder of the sponsors, while there are inconsistencies in the Commission's judgement.
Therefore, City say the sponsorship amounts were legitimate and not topped up by the owners.

articles.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga president resign over Goebbels comparison
articles.summary: Javier Tebas accuses Madrid of ‘propaganda techniques’ Club want ‘immediate resignation’ for ‘constant attacks’ Real Madrid have again demanded the resignation of the president of La Liga after he compared the club’s efforts to discredit referees with the propaganda techniques of Nazi Germany.
body: Javier Tebas lashed out at Madrid on Friday on social media with a long post that criticised how its club television channel says referees hurt its chances of winning. The channel regularly runs reels of what it considers gross errors by match officials who are set to work upcoming games for the 15-time European champions.
Tebas compared the tactic with those used by Joseph Goebbels, the minister of propaganda in Nazi Germany during the second world war.

“The executive of Real Madrid has an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid leads the way,” Tebas wrote. “Its script is always the same: select plays that favor it, repeat the alleged affront, increase suspicion and name enemies. It reminds one of the propaganda techniques that Goebbels used.”
Tebas added: “The comparison is with the techniques, not with the ideology or, of course, with Madrid fans.”

articles.title: Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director Wilcox
articles.summary: Manchester United coach accepts defender’s apology. ‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough’ Michael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez’s failure to offer Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United’s director of football in the wake of Tuesday’s…
body: Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.”

On Thursday Martínez issued an apology that did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said.

Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. “He’s released his statement, he’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough for all of us to move on with,” United’s manager said.

Carrick was pressed on whether it would have been better if Martínez had apologised to Wilcox and for his wider comments about investment, rather than just saying sorry for the timing and location of his interview. “From our point of view, the acknowledgment of what’s been done has certainly been enough, we’ve moved on and we’re definitely not looking back at it now,” he replied.

articles.title: Feel-good Koumas story something for Liverpool to smile about
articles.summary: Lewis Koumas on breaking Steven Gerrard's record, seizing his opportunity under Andoni Iraola, and why he couldn't sleep after playing Manchester City.
body: The first player to celebrate with Lewis Koumas in front of the travelling supporters in Linz was Liverpool 's hat-trick hero in Bradley Barcola.
This time last season, Koumas was on loan at Birmingham in the Championship while Barcola was at Paris St-Germain, who went on to win the Champions League for the second season in a row.
Quite a chain of events led to the pair starting together for Liverpool in their 6-3 win over LASK.

And as Barcola left the Raiffeisen Arena with the match ball after a superb hat-trick, the Frenchman knew that he wasn't the only player who put the ball in the net three times on Wednesday in Austria.

articles.title: 'Our roots are Man Utd' - but FC United ethos 'more important than ever'
articles.summary: FC United are hoping for FA Cup success, 21 years after being formed as a supporter-owned club following the Glazer family takeover of Manchester United.
body: FC United of Manchester striker Adam Le Fondre spent Tuesday lunchtime working with a group of players from the club's academy on a 3G pitch next to the club's 4,900-capacity Broadhurst Park stadium.

The dozen lads are probably not going to get anywhere near the Premier League, as Le Fondre once did, but the Northern Premier League club want to try and create a pathway to senior football, while ensuring the teenagers continue in education through their partnership with Manchester College.

Getting to train with the 39-year-old Le Fondre, scorer of more than 300 goals in professional football including 14 in his sole Premier League season, is the kind of community initiative that goes on at non-league clubs across the country.
For the people who run FC United, it is a world away from the club they once supported.

articles.title: Real Madrid lose Vinicius Junior suspension appeal as Barcelona clash looms
articles.summary: Real Madrid have failed in their appeal against Vinicius Junior’s four-match suspension, leaving the Brazilian forward set to miss the first El Clasico of the season against Barcelona.
body: The Spanish Football Federation’s (RFEF) appeals committee has upheld the punishment imposed following Vinicius’s dismissal during Madrid’s La Liga encounter with Villarreal last weekend.
The 26-year-old received a red card for pulling an opponent’s hair, with his subsequent reaction towards the referee resulting in an additional sanction.
Vinicius was handed a two-match suspension for the incident itself and another two games for his conduct after being dismissed.
Madrid challenged the decision, but the disciplinary authorities maintained that the available footage supported the referee’s account.

articles.title: United States GP: UK schedule as F1 returns to COTA
articles.summary: Following an extended stint across Asia, Formula 1 heads to America for the United States Grand Prix at the iconic Circuit of The Americas in Austin, Texas.
body: After the previous triple-header saw Kimi Antonelli move closer to a maiden F1 title, the Mercedes driver enters three more back-to-back races knowing he has every chance of sealing a historic triumph.

The Italian is 102 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell at the top of the standings, with the first two victories of the year for Red Bull and Max Verstappen only having helped Antonelli move clear of the pack, leaving him with a small chance of being crowned champion in Austin.

While both Antonelli and Mercedes are in remarkably strong positions in the championships, the competitive picture has rarely been more exciting during the 2026 season, with each of the top four teams entering each weekend with genuine hopes of victory.

Many eyes will be on Antonelli, but Verstappen's quest to complete a hat-trick of wins, along with Lewis Hamilton's attempts to bounce back from a tough Sunday in Singapore promise to provide plenty of entertainment.

articles.title: Eagles opposing player to stop, Week 6 edition
articles.summary: The Eagles are an explicit mess right now. They have had 24 players on the injury report this week. Stars Jalen Hurts, out with a serious, though treatable issue with a superficial blood clot, and Saquon Barkley will not play Sunday against the visiting Carolina Panthers.
body: What is certain is that the rising 2-2 Panthers will have Bryce Young, who has thrown for 1,268 passing yards in Carolina’s first four games, the second-most yardage thrown by a Panthers’ quarterback through four games since Cam Newton’s rookie season.

Young is beginning to turn into the player everyone envisioned him to be when he was taken No. 1 overall out of Alabama in the 2023 NFL Draft. Young has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions this season and averaging an NFL-high 317 yards passing a game, up considerably from 188.2 yards passing a game last season.

“The quarterback has really progressed,” said Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio about Young, when asked this week about what impressed him about the Panthers. “I think I coached against him when he was a rookie, and to see the progress that he’s made from then to now, kudos to him and their coaching staff. He really good processor, makes quick decisions, knows where to go with the ball. He’s elusive, he’s a scrambler, really good anticipation. Very, very impressed by him.”

articles.title: McIlroy plays just four holes of second round due to bad light in India
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy is four shots off the clubhouse lead but only four holes into his second round at the DP World India Championship after play was suspended early on Friday due to bad light in New Delhi.
body: Torrential rain on the Thursday resulted in a five-hour delay to the opening round, and there were further frustrations for those still out on the course when play was halted just before 6pm local time on Friday.

McIlroy, who is bidding to win the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, opened the tournament with a two-under 70 on Thursday, while he started his second round with an eagle to sit four under when play was stopped shortly after.

Dutchman Joost Luiten, who had to play 34 holes on Friday because of the delays, Angel Hidalgo and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship winner Adrian Meronk were all able to finish their second rounds, and top the leaderboard on eight under.
Belgian Thomas Detry is also eight under, but is only through six holes of his second round, for which he is currently three under.

articles.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
articles.summary: One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.
body: But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.
The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.
